use_case_summary: Web-based code-assistant that streams structured AST updates and tool calls into the user's editor. Needs sub-second token latency, incremental structured output so frontend can update editor progressively. Typical sessions are single-user, moderate throughput (10-30 concurrent devs max).
technical_details: Using hosted API, model 'gpt-redwood-2-large' (dev chose open model). Request pattern: streaming=true, function_call enabled with function schemas for 'apply_patch' and 'run_test'. Observed failure modes: 1) function call 'arguments' field arrives as multiple non-JSON-safe chunks (e.g., '"{\"path\": \"file.py\", \"patch\": \"diff hunk\"}"' broken across events), 2) model emits trailing commas or partial objects in intermediate deltas causing JSON.parse to throw, 3) client attempts to JSON.parse stream chunks instead of assembling complete argument payloads. Dev attempted naive concatenation + JSON.parse which fails intermittently. SE notes: reproduction uses Chrome fetch + ReadableStream reader; CORS preflight ok but frontend cannot assume complete payload per chunk.
